title: Committee of Supply − Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: Global anti-globalisation and protectionist trends
sections.summary: 2016 saw rising anti-globalisation, protectionist and nationalist sentiments, with Trump withdrawing the US from the TPP and the UK voting to leave the EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Two thousand and sixteen, though, saw several worrying trends, such as rising anti-globalisation, protectionist and nationalist sentiments, across the globe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the US, President Trump has campaigned on the back of re-negotiating or unwinding free trade agreements, including NAFTA and the TPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: He has since followed through to formally withdraw the US from the TPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Europe, the people of the UK voted to end Britain's membership of the EU, a decision which the politicians are still working hard to implement, moving through unchartered constitutional waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The polls predict that she will be the frontrunner in the first round but lose the second round.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, given that the polls were wrong on both Brexit and Trump's victory, the world may need to prepare for a scenario where she prevails in France on the back of anti-globalist sentiments.

sections.label: Singapore-China ties and leadership changes
sections.summary: Singapore set up early diplomatic ties with China in the 1990s, but leadership changes in both countries have created uncertainty about the relationship's future trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: When China was opening up to the world in the 1990s, Singapore was one of the early ones to set up formal diplomatic ties and help build bridges to ASEAN and its other friends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: However, leadership changes in both countries − namely, the election of US President Donald Trump and the upcoming 19th Party Congress of the Communist Party − have created some uncertainty about the future trajectory of this relationship.

sections.label: Trump's threatened tariff on Chinese imports
sections.summary: President Trump earlier threatened a 45% across-the-board tariff on Chinese imports, potentially leading to a difficult US-China trade relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: On the other hand, President Trump's earlier threats included a threat to slap a 45% across-the-board tariff on Chinese imports into the US, which could mean that we will potentially see a difficult trade relationship between the US and China.

sections.label: Singapore's stake in Sino-US relations
sections.summary: Singapore may face adverse consequences if US-China relations sour, and asks MFA about the direction of Sino-US relations and its strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: As a country which trades and invests extensively with both countries, Singapore may face adverse consequences if the relationship between the US and China sours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: What is MFA's take on the direction of Sino-US relations in the medium term and what is MFA's strategy to manage Singapore's relations with China and the US?

sections.label: US withdrawal from TPP
sections.summary: The new US administration pulled out of the Trans-Pacific Partnership a month ago, compounding the challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To compound this challenge, the new US administration pulled out of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) a month ago.

sections.label: US as Singapore's largest foreign investor
sections.summary: The US is Singapore's largest foreign investor, with about $244 billion in investments in 2015, accounting for 20% of inward foreign direct investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The US is also Singapore's largest foreign investor, with investments of about $244 billion in 2015, and that accounted for 20% of Singapore's foreign direct inward investments.

sections.label: Singapore US Defence Cooperation Agreement
sections.summary: In December 2015, Singapore and the US signed the enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In December 2015, Singapore and the US signed the enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA).

sections.label: Trump withdraws US from TPP
sections.summary: President Trump signed an executive order to withdraw the US from the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: President Trump has also signed an executive order to withdraw the US from the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) agreement.

sections.label: China tourists to Singapore
sections.summary: China tourists to Singapore increased to 2.86 million last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: China tourists to Singapore increased to 2.86 million last year.

sections.label: Singapore-China Joint Council cooperation
sections.summary: With the 13th Singapore-China Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation concluded, officials on both sides signalled intent to further collaborate by signing cooperation initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the conclusion of the 13th Singapore-China Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, it seems that the rough patch in Singapore-China relations in the second half of 2016 is behind us as officials on both sides signalled their intent to further collaborate by signing a series of cooperation initiatives.

sections.label: Singapore Malaysia bilateral relations upswing
sections.summary: Singapore's bilateral relations with Malaysia have seen a significant upswing in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our bilateral relations with Malaysia have seen a significant upswing in recent years.

sections.label: Malaysia seeks ICJ Pedra Branca revision
sections.summary: Malaysia's decision to apply for a revision of the ICJ's 2008 judgment on sovereignty over Pedra Branca, Middle Rocks and South Ledge was surprising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, we were surprised by Malaysia's decision to apply for a revision of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)'s 2008 judgment on the case concerning sovereignty over Pedra Branca, Middle Rocks and South Ledge.

sections.label: Singapore Indonesia bilateral relations
sections.summary: Bilateral relations with Indonesia appear to be on a positive trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Bilateral relations with Indonesia appear to be on a positive trajectory.

sections.label: Malaysia Pedra Branca ICJ application
sections.summary: Singaporeans were concerned by Malaysia's 2 February application to revise the ICJ decision awarding Pedra Branca sovereignty to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Given the excellent state of our bilateral relations, Singaporeans were naturally concerned by Malaysia's application on 2 February this year to revise the ICJ's decision which awarded sovereignty over Pedra Branca to Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore Indonesia MOUs and anniversary
sections.summary: Four MOUs were signed at the Leaders' Retreat, and Singapore and Indonesia commemorate 50 years of diplomatic relations this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In November last year, as earlier noted, four wide-ranging MOUs were signed on the sidelines of Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong's Leaders' Retreat with President Joko Widodo.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I note that Singapore and Indonesia will be commemorating their 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year.

sections.label: ASEAN land area and population
sections.summary: The 10 ASEAN countries cover about 4.4 million sq km and have approximately 625 million people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The 10 ASEAN countries cover a land area of about 4.4 million sq km and have approximately 625 million people.

sections.label: AEC, ASEAN integration, Laos Cambodia
sections.summary: The CFE Report said the AEC will make ASEAN a more compelling market and competitive production base, and Laos and Cambodia weighed national interests against ASEAN's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the CFE Report, it had mentioned that AEC will make ASEAN a more compelling market and a competitive production base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As the ASEAN Chair in 2018, how could Singapore help to advance economic integration within ASEAN and with its key partners?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: It would appear that Laos and Cambodia, which have strong overland economic ties with China, were weighing their national interests against the collective interests of ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Has this split healed since the events last year?

sections.label: Japan-Singapore Economic Partnership Agreement
sections.summary: The Japan-Singapore Economic Partnership Agreement has provided a firm foundation for economic cooperation between the two countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For instance, the Japan-Singapore Economic Partnership Agreement has provided a firm foundation for economic cooperation between our two countries.

sections.label: Singapore-Australia Joint Ministerial Committee meeting
sections.summary: The 9th Singapore-Australia Joint Ministerial Committee was held on 18 March 2016 in Sydney, led by Vivian Balakrishnan, Lim Hng Kiang and Ng Eng Hen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The 9th Singapore-Australia Joint Ministerial Committee held on 18 March 2016 in Sydney, led by Minister for Foreign Affairs Vivian Balakrishnan and Ministers Lim Hng Kiang and Ng Eng Hen, is a good example of this.

sections.label: Singapore-Australia landmark agreement
sections.summary: A May 2016 landmark agreement deepened economic integration, defence cooperation, innovation, entrepreneurship and people-to-people ties, building on the June 2015 Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We can all recollect Prime Minister Lee enjoying an outdoor BBQ session with then-Prime Minister Tony Abbot in celebrating the landmark occasion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This culminated in May 2016 when we concluded a landmark agreement to deepen economic integration, expand defence cooperation, jointly promote innovation and entrepreneurship and further strengthen our people-to-people ties by facilitating tourism, cultural exchanges and educational opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This agreement builds on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) adopted in June 2015 by the Prime Ministers of Singapore and Australia.

sections.label: Strategic uncertainties affecting Singapore
sections.summary: Strategic uncertainties from major power adjustments, such as US-China relations and Brexit, will impact Singapore, with major powers pressuring it to take sides.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Strategic uncertainties driven by the adjustment of major power relations, such as between the US and China, and Britain's exit from the EU, will impact a small country like Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A particular concern is that, from time to time, major powers will exert pressure on Singapore to take sides for a variety of reasons − nationalistic or protectionist motives, or even ethnic or religious concerns.

sections.label: South China Sea and Terrex incidents
sections.summary: The South China Sea judgment, the Terrex episode, Singapore's ASEAN-China coordinator role, a new US administration and Malaysia reopening Pedra Branca are noted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The release of the Permanent Court of Arbitration's judgment in favour of the Philippines over territorial differences in the South China Sea was followed up almost overnight by an unexpected upswing in relations between China and the Philippines even as Singapore and many like-minded countries affirmed the judgment and rule of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Terrex episode, which saw nine military vehicles temporarily confiscated by the Hong Kong authorities, hit even closer to home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would imagine these incidents, amongst many others, to have taken up much time and energy of the relevant departments in MFA and the Government more generally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is also worthwhile to note that Singapore is into its second year as country coordinator of ASEAN-China relations, a challenging assignment made even more so by a new US administration determined, on the surface at least, to take a hard-headed and transactional approach in its relationship with China and with its domestic constituency more paramount in the conduct of foreign affairs than ever before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More recently, the last few weeks have also seen the Malaysian government re-open the Pedra Branca case by way of an appeals mechanism.

sections.label: ASEAN population and GDP
sections.summary: ASEAN comprises 620 million people with an estimated combined GDP of US$2.3 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: ASEAN comprises 620 million people with an estimated combined GDP of US$2.3 trillion.

sections.label: Singapore contribution to ASEAN Trust Fund
sections.summary: Singapore recently contributed US$200,000 to the ASEAN Trust Fund for refugees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For refugees, Singapore recently contributed US$200,000 to the ASEAN Trust Fund.

sections.label: New foreign humanitarian aid department
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will consider a new department of foreign humanitarian aid to coordinate aid and regional crisis response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, will the Ministry consider establishing a new department of foreign (humanitarian) aid, similar to Japan's International Coordination Agency (JICA) or the UK's Department for International Development (DfID), for example, to coordinate humanitarian aid and strengthen our response to regional humanitarian crises?

sections.label: SCP training areas and anniversary
sections.summary: States the training covers trade promotion, healthcare, humanitarian assistance, public administration and law, and marks the SCP's 25th anniversary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The training covers various areas of interest, which include trade promotion, healthcare, humanitarian assistance, public administration and law, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This year marks the 25th anniversary of our SCP.

sections.label: Latin America trade and Mexico visit
sections.summary: States Latin America holds economic potential, Singapore's trade with Latin America and the Caribbean reached $21.1 billion in 2015, and President Tony Tan visited Mexico in June 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Latin American countries remain a very important emerging market which holds significant economic potential for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is borne out by the fact that despite a slowdown in the global economy, Singapore's trade with the Latin American and Caribbean countries reached $21.1 billion in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The region's importance to Singapore was recently underscored by President Tony Tan's state visit to Mexico in June 2016 to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Singapore and Mexico.

sections.label: Israel, Palestinians and two-state solution
sections.summary: Recounts Netanyahu's February 2017 visit, Lee's two-state solution position, a doubled $10 million Palestinian package, Maliki Osman's visit, Hawazi Daipi's appointment, and the Paris conference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Singapore in February 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: During the visit, Prime Minister Lee reiterated Singapore's longstanding and consistent position that a two-state solution is the only way to bring peace and security to the Israeli and Palestinian peoples and to the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: During his visit to the Palestinian Territories, Prime Minister Lee had announced a doubling of our enhanced technical assistance package to $10 million to support the Palestinians in building up their capacity and skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence Dr Maliki Osman followed this up with a working visit to the Palestinian Territories in November 2016, during which he informed the Palestinian leadership about the Government's appointment of Mr Hawazi Daipi as Singapore's Representative to the Palestinian National Authority to coordinate Singapore's enhanced technical assistance package for the Palestinians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Internationally, a Conference for Peace in the Middle East was also held in Paris, France, in January 2017 where there were also calls for Israel and Palestine to embrace the two-state solution.

sections.label: Consular load and lean overseas missions
sections.summary: States terror attacks and global developments will increase MFA's consular cases, public expects speedier service, and MFA has only 50 resident Overseas Missions with lean teams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We are also living in a period of greater uncertainty, as we had witnessed in the spate of terror attacks from Europe to the Middle East, and even here in Southeast Asia last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These trends and recent global developments mean that the load and complexity of consular cases that MFA has to handle will increase correspondingly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the same time, there is growing public expectation for speedier services and assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I note that MFA has only 50 resident Overseas Missions and that most Missions generally operate with very lean teams.

sections.label: MFA challenges and emergency back-up teams
sections.summary: Asks how MFA addresses challenges in unpredictable environments and whether it has regional back-up teams for large scale emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am sure that many Singaporeans who have received help from MFA in one way or another, would agree with me.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask how MFA has been addressing the challenges I mentioned earlier in the increasingly unpredictable environments we find ourselves in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Does MFA have back-up teams on standby in various regions to swing into action in the event of large scale emergencies?

sections.label: Missions and overseas Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage asks what role Singapore's Missions play in fostering ties with Singaporeans living or working overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What is the role of our Missions in fostering ties with Singaporeans living or working overseas?

sections.label: Economic headwinds and protectionism
sections.summary: The passage states that economic headwinds and global protectionist sentiments will seriously affect Singapore's trade-dependent economy, whose trade volume is three and a half times GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The economic headwinds and global protectionist sentiments are not going to go away soon and they will have serious implications on our trade-dependent economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are probably the only country where our trade volume is three and a half times our GDP.

sections.label: 2015 China agreement signed
sections.summary: The passage states that in November 2015, when President Xi Jinping came to Singapore, an agreement was signed characterising the relationship as an All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In November 2015, when President Xi Jinping came here, we signed an agreement which characterised our relationship as an "All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times".

sections.label: China ties and investment
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore believes China's success is good for China, the region and Singapore, and notes Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor and China Singapore's largest trading partner since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We do so because we believe that China's success is good, first, for the citizens of China; it is also good for the region and it is good for us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I am always amazed that tiny Singapore currently is China's largest foreign investor, and we have been so since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: China is Singapore's largest trading partner also since 2013.

sections.label: Chongqing Connectivity Initiative project
sections.summary: The passage states the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative, the third Government-to-Government project, is a priority demonstration project for the Belt and Road and will link Western China to Southeast Asia and Central Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our third and latest Government-to-Government project, the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative, has been designated a priority demonstration project for the "Belt and Road", and will play a catalytic role in linking up Western China − both to Southeast Asia, as well as across to Central Asia and beyond.

sections.label: US-Singapore economic ties
sections.summary: The passage states the US is Singapore's fourth largest goods trading partner, top services trading partner and largest foreign direct investor, and Singapore is the US' fourth largest Asian investor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On the economic front, the US is Singapore's fourth largest trading partner in goods and our top trading partner in services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The US is also Singapore's largest foreign direct investor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore is the US' fourth largest Asian investor, after Japan, Australia and the ROK.

sections.label: KL-Singapore High Speed Rail agreement
sections.summary: The Agreement on the KL-Singapore High Speed Rail was signed in December 2016, reaching a milestone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: More recently, we reached a milestone by signing the Agreement on the KL-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) in December 2016.

sections.label: Singapore-JB Rapid Transit System agreement
sections.summary: Singapore is looking to sign a bilateral agreement on the Singapore-JB Rapid Transit System this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In addition to the HSR, we are also looking to sign a bilateral agreement on this Singapore-JB Rapid Transit System (RTS) this year.

sections.label: ICJ Pedra Branca judgment and revision
sections.summary: The ICJ's 2008 judgment assigned sovereignty over Pedra Branca, Middle Rocks and South Ledge, and Malaysia applied for revision in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In its judgment dated 23 May 2008, the ICJ found that sovereignty over Pedra Branca belonged to Singapore, sovereignty over Middle Rocks belonged to Malaysia and sovereignty over South Ledge belonged to the state in the territorial waters of which it is located.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On 2 February 2017, Malaysia applied for a revision of the judgment under Article 61 of the ICJ's Statute.

sections.label: Rebuttal to Malaysia's ICJ application
sections.summary: Singapore's legal team believes Malaysia's documents do not meet Article 61 criteria and will submit its rebuttal by 14 June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our legal team strongly believes that the documents relied on by Malaysia do not satisfy the criteria under Article 61.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will submit to the ICJ our comprehensive and compelling rebuttal to Malaysia's application by 14 June, which is the time limit fixed by the ICJ.

sections.label: Eastern Boundary Treaty ratification exchange
sections.summary: The Indonesian Foreign Minister and the speaker announced celebrations and marked the exchange of instruments of ratification for the Eastern Boundary Treaty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Indonesian Foreign Minister, Ibu Retno Marsudi, and I announced the start of the celebrations last month during her official visit to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also marked a milestone in bilateral relations through the exchange of instruments of ratification for the Eastern Boundary Treaty on 10 February 2017.

sections.label: ASEAN as Singapore's foreign policy anchor
sections.summary: ASEAN is Singapore's anchor and a cornerstone of its foreign policy, with projected economic and demographic growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In an often turbulent world, ASEAN is, as Mr Low puts it, Singapore's anchor and a cornerstone of our foreign policy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are now already the seventh largest economy in the world and, barring any mishaps, we are projected to become the fourth largest economy by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Today, we have 628 million people, our combined GDP is US$2.5 trillion and, sometime between 2030 and 2050, we hope that this will quadruple to US$10 trillion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: What is important also is that we will have the third largest labour force in the world and, more important than that, more than half the population of ASEAN is under the age of 30.

sections.label: ASEAN-China relations and South China Sea
sections.summary: Singapore upgraded the ASEAN-China FTA in 2015 and will advance connectivity and the Code of Conduct during its coordinatorship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We upgraded the ASEAN-China FTA in 2015 and we facilitated a successful and substantive ASEAN-China 25th Anniversary Commemorative Summit last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will continue advancing other initiatives, such as enhancing connectivity and making progress on the Code of Conduct in the South China Sea, in the remaining one and a half years of our coordinatorship.

sections.label: SAF training access in Australia
sections.summary: The MOU on Military Training and Training Area Development gives the SAF enhanced access to Australian training areas for 25 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The MOU on Military Training and Training Area Development gives the SAF significant enhanced access to training areas in Australia over the next 25 years.

sections.label: EU-Singapore FTA engagement
sections.summary: Singapore continues engaging Europe and the EU through the EU-Singapore FTA, delayed by legal hurdles but supported by engaged European countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Brexit notwithstanding, we continue to engage Europe and the EU, for example, through the EU-Singapore FTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Yes, it has been delayed by certain legal hurdles that we have to go through, but, so far, all the countries that we have engaged in Europe have expressed support for this FTA.

sections.label: Trade arrangements and economic partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore will pursue RCEP, the ASEAN Economic Community, and ways to take the TPP forward despite US withdrawal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These arrangements increase opportunities for Singapore companies and Singapore to do more in the face of a world which is sometimes at risk of insularism and protectionism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will work towards the expeditious conclusion of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) and continue to pursue further development of the ASEAN Economic Community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will explore ways to take the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) forward, despite the US' withdrawal.

sections.label: Technical assistance to developing countries
sections.summary: Singapore contributes to the multilateral system by training over 112,000 officials from other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also contribute to the multilateral system through technical assistance to developing countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I think we have trained over 112,000 officials from many other countries because they want to understand how Singapore works and how these lessons can be brought back home.

sections.label: Terrorist threats and consular assistance
sections.summary: MFA and MHA will monitor security and terrorist threats and strengthen consular assistance for Singaporeans overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This is evidenced by high-profile attacks in parts of Europe and Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are actually at even higher risk, even as ISIS loses its stronghold in the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: MFA and MHA will continue to monitor security and terrorist threats, and we stand ready to assist Singaporeans in distress overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have had Singaporeans injured or otherwise involved in terrorist incidents overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: One of our top challenges is to strengthen our consular assistance.

sections.label: Singapore foreign policy commitment
sections.summary: MFA will enhance Singapore's relevance, maintain an independent and principled foreign policy, and work with Members to build appreciation of foreign policy hard truths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: MFA will continue to enhance Singapore's long-term value proposition and relevance to other countries; we will maintain our commitment to an independent and principled foreign policy in a rules-based global order; we will continue to work with all Members of this House to build a deeper appreciation of the hard truths that underpin our foreign policy.

sections.label: Visits by new leaders
sections.summary: Last year Singapore hosted visits by newly inaugurated leaders from the Philippines, Vietnam and Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Last year, we hosted visits by newly inaugurated leaders such as Philippines President Rodrigo Duterte, Vietnam President Tran Dai Quang and Myanmar State Counsellor Daw Aung San Suu Kyi.

sections.label: ASEAN visa requirements lifted
sections.summary: Singapore and Myanmar mutually lifted visa requirements last December, and there are now no visa requirements for all ASEAN nationals travelling to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, Singapore and Myanmar mutually lifted visa requirements last December.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are now no visa requirements for all ASEAN nationals travelling to Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore-China investment and trade
sections.summary: Since 2013, Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor and China Singapore's largest trading partner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since 2013, Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor and China our largest trading partner.

sections.label: Belt and Road cooperation areas
sections.summary: At the JCBC meeting, both sides agreed China's Belt and Road initiative presents new areas for cooperation such as infrastructure development and third-country capacity building.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the JCBC meeting, both sides agreed that China's Belt and Road initiative presents new areas for fruitful cooperation, such as in infrastructure development and third-country capacity building.

sections.label: Singapore missions and engagements in China
sections.summary: MFA has one embassy and four consulates-general in mainland China, the highest number of overseas missions in a single country, with unmatched high-level visits and consultations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In MFA since late 2015, I now see the intensity of our engagements from another lens.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have one embassy and four consulates-general in mainland China, which is the highest number of overseas missions we have in a single country.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The regularity of high-level visits and the frequency of bilateral consultations with China are also unmatched by any other country.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, the China-Singapore Forum on Leadership was launched in 2009 and has held five meetings thus far.

sections.label: Bilateral cooperation with China
sections.summary: Singapore-China relations include three G-to-G projects and three high-level bilateral mechanisms, and have kept up with the times and China's changing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The depth and intensity of our bilateral cooperation, which includes the three G-to-G projects and three high-level bilateral mechanisms, underscores the fundamental point that our relations have always kept up with the times, taking into account China's changing needs.

sections.label: Southern Transport Corridor
sections.summary: The Southern Transport Corridor links Chongqing to the ASEAN region via Beibu Gulf in Guangxi and can connect the overland Silk Route Economic Belt and the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, the Southern Transport Corridor linking Chongqing to the ASEAN region via Beibu Gulf in Guangxi can help connect the overland Silk Route Economic Belt and the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road.

sections.label: EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement
sections.summary: Singapore hopes the EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement will be ratified so both sides can benefit, while the EU has its own domestic preoccupations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While the EU has its own domestic preoccupations, we are hopeful that the EU-Singapore Free Trade Agree (EUSFTA) will be ratified so that both sides can benefit from it.

sections.label: No separate humanitarian assistance agency
sections.summary: At this juncture, Singapore prefers not to divert further resources to set up a separate department or agency for humanitarian assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At this juncture, we prefer not to divert further resources to set up a separate department or agency for humanitarian assistance.

sections.label: Singapore Cooperation Programme anniversary
sections.summary: The SCP marks its 25th Anniversary, running over 300 programmes yearly for about 6,500 officials from over 170 countries, with over 112,000 foreign officials having participated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This year marks the 25th Anniversary of the SCP, our primary platform for sharing our developmental experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We now run, on average, more than 300 programmes for some 6,500 government officials from over 170 countries annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the 25 years, more than 112,000 foreign officials have participated in the SCP.

sections.label: Initiative for ASEAN Integration upgrade
sections.summary: Singapore is offering capacity building beyond classroom training under the IAI and plans to upgrade IAI centres in Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and Myanmar to Singapore Cooperation Centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Closer to home, we are increasing our efforts to help fellow ASEAN countries bridge the development gap by offering capacity building beyond traditional classroom training under the Initiative for ASEAN Integration (IAI).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We plan to upgrade the current IAI centres in Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and Myanmar to integrated development platforms called "Singapore Cooperation Centres".

sections.label: Ethiopia and Sub-Saharan Africa opportunities
sections.summary: Ethiopia has averaged 10% growth over the last decade, and MFA and MTI are exploring economic opportunities in Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Far from its earlier years of being known as a famine-stricken country, Ethiopia has enjoyed growth rates averaging 10% over the last decade and is now one of the world's top 10 fastest growing economies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: MFA is working with MTI to explore economic opportunities in other parts of Sub-Saharan Africa in sectors like commodities, logistics, port development, urban solutions and information communications and technology.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We currently have some 60 Singapore-based companies with business operations in over 40 Sub-Saharan Africa countries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This number is likely to grow in the coming years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are also making good progress in Latin America, where our trade has more than doubled over the past decade and about 130 companies are now doing business there.

sections.label: EAEU and Turkey-Singapore FTA
sections.summary: The EAEU has a combined market of 179 million people and a GDP of US$4.4 trillion, and the Turkey-Singapore FTA is expected to be ratified this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Comprising Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, the EAEU has a combined market of 179 million people and a GDP of US$4.4 trillion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The Turkey-Singapore FTA, which is expected to be ratified this year, will allow our companies to leverage Turkey's strategic location to pursue investments in Central Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

sections.label: Singapore position on Israel-Palestine
sections.summary: Singapore has urged Israel and Palestine to resume direct negotiations and work towards a just and durable solution, convinced a two-state solution is the only way to peace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Despite Singapore's close relations with Israel, we have taken a principled, consistent and long-standing position on the Israel-Palestine issue.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Although the situation is complex and progress is difficult, Singapore has always urged Israel and Palestine to resume direct negotiations and work towards a just and durable solution to this long-standing conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This is because we are convinced that a two-state solution for Israel and Palestine, however hard to achieve, is the only way to bring peace and security to both peoples.

sections.label: Doubling ETAP to PNA
sections.summary: During the Prime Minister's visit to Ramallah in April last year, he announced the doubling of the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package to the PNA from S$5 million to S$10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: During the Prime Minister's visit to Ramallah in April last year, he also announced the doubling of our Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP) to the PNA from S$5 million to S$10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The SCP has trained over 260 Palestinian officials in various courses over the years.

sections.summary: Even as ISIS loses ground, returning fighters pose a long-term threat, with more than 1,000 Indonesians, Malaysians, Filipinos and Singaporeans having gone to fight for ISIS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: However, even as ISIS loses ground, returning fighters continue to pose a long-term threat to global security, as pointed out by several counter-terrorism experts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This region is not immune, with more than 1,000 Indonesians, Malaysians, Filipinos and even Singaporeans having gone to fight for ISIS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Within 24 hours, the deceased and injured were repatriated back to Singapore.

sections.label: MFA e-Register travel urging
sections.summary: Singaporeans are urged to e-Register with MFA when travelling, given the disparity between 400,000 e-registrants and 7.5 million outbound trips in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Importantly, we urge Singaporeans to e-Register with MFA when travelling, either through our MFA website or the MFA@SG app.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: There is a huge disparity between the 400,000 e-registrants we have on record and the 7.5 million outbound trips made by Singaporeans via air and sea in 2016 and this excludes the over 16 million overland travels to Malaysia annually.

sections.label: Emergency calls from next-of-kin
sections.summary: About eight out of 10 calls MFA receives during emergencies come from next-of-kin of Singaporeans who did not e-register.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Currently, about eight out of 10 calls that MFA receives during emergency situations are from the next-of-kin of Singaporeans who did not e-register.

sections.label: Stranded youth football team assistance
sections.summary: MFA worked with SIA to help a stranded 13-member youth football team and some parents depart Antalya for Gothenburg in time for the Gothia World Youth Cup 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As a 13-member youth football team and some of their parents were also stranded in Antalya due to the closure of the Istanbul airport, MFA worked with SIA to facilitate their departure from Antalya to Gothenburg, Sweden, so that they could arrive in time for the Gothia World Youth Cup 2016.

sections.label: MFA aid and diplomacy clarifications
sections.summary: A message credits MFA's aid for a family's safe return, and clarifications concern rules-based versus power-based diplomacy and possible ASEAN Summit difficulties with the Philippines as Chair.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: But what keeps the officers going is the knowledge that they are helping fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: He wrote, "When I contacted MFA to get more information on the unfortunate bus crash, not only did they give me the information I needed, it was because of the aid MFA rendered that my family was able to return safely to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We would not have been able to go through this on our own and we will always remember how MFA had our back.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The MFA team was professional, polite and considerate even when we were in so much distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: First, while Singapore believes in rules-based diplomacy, other countries Singapore has to deal with may believe in power-based diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: The second clarification is whether the Minister anticipates difficulties in this year's ASEAN Summit with the Philippines as the Chair of ASEAN?

sentences.text: The ultimate challenge in international law is enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Member's second point was on ASEAN Chairmanship.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I would express full support for the Chairmanship of ASEAN under the Philippines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In relation to China, I also see some seeds of opportunities because in recent months China has actually been talking about the importance of holding up environmental legislation.

sections.label: Consulates upgrade in Indonesia
sections.summary: Plans are to upgrade consulates in Batam and Medan, with other plans not yet announceable, and MFA also uses non-resident Ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Do we have similar plans for Southeast Asia and other regions of interest in general?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think what I can say today is that we are planning to upgrade our consulates in Batam and Medan, because more people and more businesses are passing or transacting through Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Although we do have some other plans, I am not in the position to announce yet.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Again, I think the Member's larger point is that the demands on MFA are growing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I hope Members noticed that, in fact, our budget for this year is actually a bit less than last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I do not say this in a facetious way, for it just illustrates how hard our staff are working.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: There is also another secret recipe that we have, that is, we also have a system of non-resident Ambassadors.

sections.label: Singapore relationships and small MFA budget
sections.summary: Singapore has meaningful relationships with many countries, and its small Ministry of 50 officers makes the most of its budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I think every continent except Antarctica − but there is a story there as well, I believe, which we just have not had time to share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: But the fact that Singapore as a small country has meaningful relationships with so many countries, is truly an achievement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In true Singapore tradition, you deliver value-for-money, so it is a very small budget Ministry, 50 officers, but we make the most of what we have.
